title: Entrusted on-prem packaged bundles and deferred upgrade path experiment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We are prototyping an alternative on-prem licensing package targeted at mid-market and enterprise customers that require VPC/on-prem isolation. The experiment combines an 'Entrusted Bundle' (annual license fee + optional ops/support bands + migration credits) with a deferred upgrade pathway that allows customers to opt into a predictable upgrade window for major platform releases. The goal is to strike a balance between revenue predictability, security assurance for buyers, and reduced operational lift for Redwood engineering/support.

Motivation: Sales teams report deal friction around rigid upgrade cadences and license fees that don't reflect real consumption patterns for large customers with long validation cycles (security questionnaires, air-gapped approval, compliance windows). Engineering/SRE are seeing high churn in emergency patch requests and bespoke upgrade branches for customers on indefinite maintenance windows.

Proposed experiment design:
- Offer two pilot SKUs to 3 strategic customers:
  - SKU A (Entrusted Flat): higher annual license fee, tiered ops/support bands (Bronze/Silver/Gold), includes 2 scheduled Major Upgrades/year inside pre-agreed 6-week maintenance windows, emergency patch SLA at Gold.
  - SKU B (Entrusted Elastic): lower base fee + maintenance credits that offset up to X% of upgrade/service engineering hours; customers can bank credits for deferred upgrades into a quarterly upgrade window. Includes security questionnaire pre-clear bundle (KMS/HSM attestations, audit logs, data isolation checklist).
- Contract terms and SOWs will include explicit upgrade cadence options, rollback & escrow clauses, and failure/recovery acceptance criteria.

Success metrics:
- Primary: Lift in close velocity for pilot cohort (expected +25% faster contract cycles), and ARR uplift vs baseline packaging (+15% ARR on average for pilot customers).
- Secondary: Reduction in ad-hoc emergency engineering hours (target -40%), decreased number of bespoke upgrade branches, improved average time-to-complete security questionnaire (target -30%).

Trade-offs and risks:
- Revenue risk if deferred upgrades delay recognition. We'll model revenue deferral in contract templates and offer migration credits as financed incentives.
- Engineering operational risk if too many customers choose deferred windows; mitigate by capacity reservations and scheduled upgrade cadence enforcement in dedicated pool booking.
- Compliance & legal risk around escrow and KMS attestations; requires coordination with Security and Legal for acceptable wording and proof artifacts.

Artifacts and links:
- PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Entrusted+Onprem+Packaging+PRD
- Contract templates & SOW examples: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A_EntrustedContracts
- Security questionnaire checklist (working): https://docs.redwood.ai/security/entrusted-q-checklist
- Pilot customer tracker (internal): https://sheets.redwood.ai/d/entrusted-pilot

Notes on pricing model calculations: attached spreadsheet models three scenarios (conservative/expected/aggressive) and sensitivity to average support hours per year. The prototype assumes Gold band has 24x7 on-call with 4-hour emergency patch SLA and is priced as a percentage uplift over base license.
